sections.body: The AI Researcher covers the places where artificial intelligence has moved into the daily work of scholarship, from the first literature search to the final peer review. In practice this means systems that retrieve and rank papers, tools that extract claims and findings from full texts, and models that draft, summarise, translate, or check writing. It also means software that runs statistical pipelines, codes interview transcripts, schedules instruments, and simulates experiments that would be slow or costly at the bench.The work is less about a machine making a discovery on its own and more about compressing the reading, counting, and drafting that surrounds a study.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Retrieval and summarisation are the most mature parts of this field, and citation mapping is largely a solved navigation problem, though coverage gaps and errors in metadata persist. Quantitative pipelines are reproducible when the code and data are shared, and that sharing remains the exception rather than the rule. Qualitative coding with AI is useful for triage and consistency checks but struggles with context, irony, and the tacit knowledge that makes interpretation defensible. Peer review and grant assessment are being assisted, not replaced, and the honest limits are clear: models can fabricate references, flatten disagreement, and inherit bias from the literature they were trained on. Governance and integrity rules are still catching up to tools that are already in wide use.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader starts with Literature Review and Evidence Synthesis for how search and screening are being automated, then moves to Citation Mapping and Discovery to see how citation networks reveal influence and gaps. Quantitative Analysis and Reproducible Work and Qualitative Analysis and Mixed Methods split the analysis side, one for statistics and code, the other for text, interviews, and mixed designs. Grant Proposals and Funding and Academic Writing and Peer Review cover the writing and assessment stages, including where drafting help ends and authorship questions begin. Course Design and Teaching turns to the classroom, while Research Data and Repositories and Laboratory Automation and Simulation handle storage, sharing, instruments, and simulated experiments. Governance, Ethics and Research Integrity sits underneath all of them, because the rules about disclosure, bias, and accountability apply to every page in this section.
